policy.source_reference: data/Document 2 — Ryde Dispute Resolution Policy v2.1 (Markdown).md

clauses.text: Section 2.1: Five-minute free wait from scheduled pickup time. Early arrival earns no pre-schedule credit. Implementation interpretation: a late driver must also spend five physical minutes at pickup after arrival.
Section 2.2: A valid driver-cancelled rider no-show incurs SGD 5.00, transferred to the driver as compensation.
Section 2.3: Before cancellation, driver must send at least one in-app chat message AND attempt at least one in-app phone call. Failure of either obligation voids the fee.

Section 2.4: Driver must arrive by scheduled pickup plus 5 minutes. Rider may cancel at no charge when driver fails this arrival condition. Driver no-show plus no contact qualifies for a separate SGD 5 goodwill credit.
Section 2.5: At least 3 no-show cancellations within a rolling 30 days flag the rider for human account review; do not suspend accounts or infer fee validity from history.

Precedent 7.3, DISP-2026-0211: Driver waited 6 minutes but made no message or call. SGD 5 cancellation fee reversed. Relevant when contact obligations are missing; it is not the answer label for the current case.
Section 5.1–5.2: Safety indicators in any dispute require immediate human review. AI must not issue rulings, assign fault, or recommend a resolution for safety incidents.
Section 6.1: Dispute value under SGD 10 permits any confidence; SGD 10–50 needs at least 80%; above SGD 50 requires human review.
Section 6.2: Route AI rulings require confidence >=80% and additional distance <=2 km. No-show/cancellation fee is fixed at SGD 5; safety is always escalated. Unsupported categories are referred.

Section 6.3: Confidence considers evidence completeness, policy clarity, precedent alignment and credibility. Any party fraud flag >=1 raises the confidence requirement to 95%; a flag does not establish fault.

clauses.text: Section 1.1: Rerouting for traffic, road closures or congestion is permitted, but the rider must be informed.
Section 1.2: Inform rider via in-app chat or recorded call before or at deviation; a brief reason is sufficient.

Section 1.3: The no-refund tolerance is 1 km of additional distance. For additional distance above 1 km, apply these separate cases. UNJUSTIFIED detour: refund ALL excess-distance fare; the formula is additional km multiplied by the distance rate. This refunds a fare component, not the entire trip or time-charge difference. JUSTIFIED detour with timely rider notification and agreement: no refund. JUSTIFIED but UNNOTIFIED detour: refund only PART of the excess-distance fare; that partial-component formula is unspecified, so refer until confirmed. The unspecified formula applies only to the justified-but-unnotified case and never to an unjustified detour.

policy.source_reference: data/Document 2 — Ryde Dispute Resolution Policy v2.1 (Markdown).md

clauses.text: Section 1.1: Rerouting for traffic, road closures or congestion is permitted, but the rider must be informed.
Section 1.2: Inform rider via in-app chat or recorded call before or at deviation; a brief reason is sufficient.

Section 1.3: The no-refund tolerance is 1 km of additional distance. For additional distance above 1 km, apply these separate cases. UNJUSTIFIED detour: refund ALL excess-distance fare; the formula is additional km multiplied by the distance rate. This refunds a fare component, not the entire trip or time-charge difference. JUSTIFIED detour with timely rider notification and agreement: no refund. JUSTIFIED but UNNOTIFIED detour: refund only PART of the excess-distance fare; that partial-component formula is unspecified, so refer until confirmed. The unspecified formula applies only to the justified-but-unnotified case and never to an unjustified detour.

Section 1.4: Additional km = actual minus recommended distance. Traffic justification uses historical traffic API records for the segment at trip time. Chat/call acknowledgment establishes agreement. App alert words alone are insufficient.

Precedent 7.1, DISP-2026-0089: 1.8 km traffic-justified detour without notification; partial excess-distance refund SGD 3.20, confidence 91%. The amount does not define a general percentage or formula.
Section 5.1–5.2: Safety indicators in any dispute require immediate human review. AI must not issue rulings, assign fault, or recommend a resolution for safety incidents.
Section 6.1: Dispute value under SGD 10 permits any confidence; SGD 10–50 needs at least 80%; above SGD 50 requires human review.
Section 6.2: Route AI rulings require confidence >=80% and additional distance <=2 km. No-show/cancellation fee is fixed at SGD 5; safety is always escalated. Unsupported categories are referred.

Section 6.3: Confidence considers evidence completeness, policy clarity, precedent alignment and credibility. Any party fraud flag >=1 raises the confidence requirement to 95%; a flag does not establish fault.

The driver also failed to provide timely notice or obtain rider agreement before deviating.

The rider initiated the conversation asking why the route changed, and the driver provided a reason (traffic) immediately after the deviation started, satisfying the notification requirement for a justified detour even if the final justification is unverified.

Since historical traffic data confirms no congestion for the segment, the route deviation lacks objective justification, making the refund obligation determined by whether the rider was informed/agreed, which the system flags as false.

Without verified traffic justification and lacking pre-deviation notification, the detour falls into the unjustified or unjustified-unnotified category where the driver is liable for the full excess distance fare.
